source.reason: b0014 states the designed steel 'has been developed by melting-casting route in an open-air induction furnance (Power Trak 250-10 R Inductotherm)'. This is the only processing step that creates the as-cast specimen state.

method.value: melting-casting route in an open-air induction furnace (Power Trak 250-10 R Inductotherm)

processing_steps_notes.value: The developed steel was produced by the conventional melting-casting route in an open-air induction furnace; the as-solidified cast ingot constitutes the cast specimen (state_label 'cast specimen'). No further thermal/mechanical step is applied to this state.

source.reason: The cast specimen is characterized as a dual-phase δ-ferrite + austenite structure with dendritic austenite (XRD and optical microscopy, Fig. 2).

overall_structure.value: Dual-phase microstructure of delta ferrite (δ) and austenite (γ) in the cast specimen, confirmed by XRD and optical microscopy; the austenite in the cast specimen has a dendritic type structure.

source.reason: b0036 reports that XRD (Fig. 2a) and optical images (Fig. 2b,c) confirm a dual-phase microstructure in the cast specimen with dendritic austenite; the quantified austenite fraction of ~26 vol% is for the cast sample.
XRD of the cast specimen shows ferrite and austenite, presumed to be δ-ferrite based on the Thermo-Calc plot [b0036]; the paper states a higher fraction of δ-ferrite '~70 (volume%)' [b0037].

b0036 states ~26% (volume %) austenite in the cast sample (Rietveld refinement of XRD) and that the austenite in the cast specimen has a dendritic type structure. Fig. 2 confirms γ (austenite) peaks in XRD.

The only intrinsic physical property reported for the developed steel (base = cast) is the Archimedes density; tensile/hardness data are only reported for HRQ and annealed specimens, so mechanical slots are left empty for the cast state.

b0034 reports, based on Archimedes' principle, that the developed steel (of which the cast specimen is the base state) has a density of 6.91455 g/cc. Not attributed to any specific processing state in the text.

b0017 describes the XRD setup; b0036 reports that XRD analysis was conducted on samples after casting and hot forging and shows ferrite and austenite in the cast specimen; b0040/Fig. 2a gives the cast XRD pattern and peak indices.

instrument_or_setup.value: Bruker D8 advanced X-ray diffractometer, Co-Kα (1.79 Å) target

purpose.value: To identify the major phases present in the developed steel after casting (and hot forging)

key_findings.value: XRD of the cast specimen (Fig. 2a, black pattern) shows the presence of ferrite and austenite; reflections indexed α110, γ111, γ200, α200, γ220, α211, γ311 and γ222 (α: ferrite (δ/α), γ: austenite).

source.reason: b0017 describes optical microscopy and specimen preparation; b0036 reports the optical images of the cast specimen (Fig. 2b,c) confirming dual-phase dendritic austenite.

purpose.value: To confirm the phases/microstructure of the cast specimen

key_findings.value: Optical images (Fig. 2b,c) confirm a dual-phase microstructure in the cast specimen; the austenite in the cast specimen has a dendritic type structure (indicated by blue arrow in Fig. 2b,c).

source.reason: b0036 states the volume fraction of phases was calculated by Rietveld refinement using XRD data, giving ~26% austenite in the cast sample.

purpose.value: To calculate the volume fraction of phases in the cast specimen

key_findings.value: ~26% (volume %) of austenite in the cast sample; unchanged to ~29% in the forged sample, showing only ~3% difference.

source.reason: b0033 describes the Thermo-Calc equilibrium phase-fraction plot (database TCFE9) used to predict critical temperatures and phase fractions of the developed steel; this underpins the identification of δ-ferrite in the cast specimen. Applies to the alloy (cast is its base state).

boundary_and_initial_conditions.value: Equilibrium phase fractions versus temperature (Fig. 1b); duplex ferrite (δ) + austenite (γ) region measured to be ~650 °C to ~1350 °C; equilibrium transformation sequence L → L+δ → L+δ+γ → γ+δ; BCC phase remains on cooling from liquid (>~1500 °C) to room temperature.

validation_against_experiment.value: Used to identify that ferrite present in the cast specimen is δ-ferrite; dilatometry conducted on the forged sample showed no significant transformation-related contraction, consistent with the thermocalc prediction.

source.reason: The paper performs thermodynamic/SFE computations for the developed alloy; the cast specimen is the base state of this alloy.

boundary_and_initial_conditions.value: Variables include grain size (initial finer austenite grain assumed 40 µm), temperature and alloy composition; interfacial surface energy σ^{γ/ε} taken as 10 mJ/m² (literature range 5-15 mJ/m²).

source.reason: b0021-b0032 derive the SFE of the developed steel using the Olson and Cohen thermodynamic model and report the parameters and the resulting ~35 mJ/m².

equation_role.value: γ_SFE = 2ρΔG^{γ→ε} + 2σ^{γ/ε}, with ΔG^{γ→ε} = ΔG_chem + ΔG_mag + ΔG_ex

model_note.value: The theoretical SFE of the designed steel is ~35 mJ/m² (within the 20-40 mJ/m² TWIP range). This computation is for the designed alloy (cast is its base state).

unmapped_findings: Measured bulk chemical composition of the developed steel (Table 1, wt.%): Fe bal., Mn 7.79, Al 4.88, Si 0.84, C 0.2, P 0.03, S 0.03; measured by XRF and OES (b0014, b0016).
The designed grade is Fe-8Mn-5Al-0.2C (wt.%) low-density medium Mn steel; the cast specimen is the as-solidified state of this alloy (b0014).
The developed steel shows ~11.35% density reduction compared to conventional steel (~7.8 g/cc), achieved by the addition of ~5 (wt.%) Al and ~1 (wt.%) Si (b0034).
XRD of the cast specimen (Fig. 2a, black 'Cast Specimen' pattern) is indexed with reflections α110, γ111, γ200, α200, γ220, α211, γ311 and γ222; legend 'α: ferrite (δ/α), γ: austenite' (figure_002).
